accepted.s: Vira Narasimha entered into an alliance with which Portuguese Viceroy for securing horses and military training?
accepted.x: Vira Narasimha allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida for horses and military training.
accepted.tq: Identify the person directly associated with the stated diplomatic and military arrangement.
accepted.sec: Relations with the Portuguese - Albuquerque, Goa, horse trade

accepted.s: In 1510, Krishnadevaraya supported Albuquerque's capture of Goa from Bijapur through which envoy?
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya backed Albuquerque's capture of Goa through the envoy Luis in 1510.
accepted.tq: Use the date and envoy-name combination to distinguish closely related Portuguese figures.
accepted.sec: Relations with the Portuguese - Albuquerque, Goa, horse trade

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a consequence of Krishnadevaraya's support to Albuquerque in the capture of Goa?
o: Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
Transfer of Raichur to the Portuguese
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya received horses and training and permitted the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal. Transfer of Raichur to the Portuguese was not a stated consequence.
accepted.tq: Find the option that changes a military and commercial arrangement into an unsupported territorial transfer.
accepted.sec: Relations with the Portuguese - Albuquerque, Goa, horse trade

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Portuguese assistance to Vijayanagara:
1. Portuguese engineers built the Nagalapuram tank.
2. Portuguese engineers built the Toragallu dam.
3. Portuguese help was useful at Raichur in 1520.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Portuguese engineers constructed the Nagalapuram tank and Toragallu dam, and Portuguese assistance counted at Raichur in 1520.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the connected list of engineering and military contributions.
accepted.sec: Relations with the Portuguese - Albuquerque, Goa, horse trade

accepted.s: Who made peace after Sadasiva and Rama Raya defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples?
accepted.x: João de Castro made peace after the defeat of Martin de Souza, whose actions had included damaging temples.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish Portuguese governors and peace-makers.
accepted.sec: Relations with the Portuguese - Albuquerque, Goa, horse trade

accepted.s: Achyutaraya, who succeeded Krishnadevaraya, ruled during which period?
accepted.x: Achyutaraya ruled from 1529 to 1542.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adjacent reigns by matching the ruler with the precise regnal years.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the coronation of Achyutaraya is correct?
1. He was named heir by Krishnadevaraya.
2. He was crowned at Tirupati and Srikalahasti.
3. He was the only king crowned at Tirumala.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Achyutaraya was named heir by Krishnadevaraya and was crowned at Tirupati and Srikalahasti. He is identified as the only king crowned at Tirumala.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying the succession and coronation details separately.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: During the reign of Achyutaraya, real power was largely exercised by whom?
accepted.x: Real power during Achyutaraya's reign lay with his brothers-in-law, the Salakam brothers.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with the family group that actually exercised power.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: Fernao Nuniz visited Vijayanagara during the reign of which ruler?
accepted.x: Although Nuniz described Krishnadevaraya's rise to power, he visited Vijayanagara under Achyutaraya.
accepted.tq: Separate the ruler described in an account from the ruler during whose reign the visitor actually arrived.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: Aliya Rama Raya was related to Krishnadevaraya as his:
o: maternal uncle from the Gajapati family
younger brother from the Tuluva family
accepted.x: Aliya Rama Raya was Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and belonged to the Aravidu family.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between relationship and dynastic affiliation rather than relying on the title alone.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s:
Which sequence correctly represents the events associated with Aliya Rama Raya?
A. Sadasiva was made a figurehead king
B. Salakam Tirumala was killed
C. Rama Raya was beheaded at Talikota
D. Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda
accepted.x: Rama Raya killed Salakam Tirumala in 1543, made Sadasiva a figurehead king, was beheaded at Talikota in 1565, and thereafter Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda.
accepted.tq: Fix the dated event first and then place the consequences in their logical sequence.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: Rama Raya's policy of divide and rule was directed against the:
accepted.x: Rama Raya used divide and rule against the Deccan Sultanates, which eventually united against him.
accepted.tq: Identify the political group affected by the stated strategy and its eventual reaction.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: The battle of Talikota, also known as Rakshasi-Tangadi or Bannihatti, was fought in:

accepted.tq: Distinguish the battle's alternative names from the precise date of its occurrence.
accepted.sec: Achyutaraya and Sadasivaraya - Rama Raya's regency

accepted.s: Who is identified as having beheaded Rama Raya at the battle of Talikota?
accepted.x: Rama Raya was beheaded at Talikota by Hussain Nizam Shah.
accepted.tq: Use the person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish the combatant from the fleeing rulers.

accepted.s: Nagalapuram was named after:
accepted.x: Nagalapuram was named after Krishnadevaraya's mother, Nagalamba.

accepted.s:
Which of the following was the correct sequence of the principal stages in Krishnadevaraya's campaign against Prataparudra Gajapati?
A. Udayagiri
B. Kondaveedu
C. Kondapalli and Bejawada
D. March to Cuttack
accepted.x: The campaign proceeded through Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Bejawada, followed by the march to Cuttack in 1518.
accepted.tq: Arrange the campaign stages geographically and sequentially from the first fort to Cuttack.
accepted.sec: Wars and peace with Prataparudra Gajapati - battles, terms  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the terms of peace between Krishnadevaraya and Prataparudra Gajapati?
o: Permanent annexation of all Gajapati territories south of the Krishna
Marriage of Prataparudra's daughter to Krishnadevaraya
Return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati
accepted.x: The terms included a marriage alliance, the Balakrishna idol, and return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati. Permanent annexation of all Gajapati territories south of the Krishna was not stated.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme territorial claim when testing a list of treaty terms.
accepted.sec: Wars and peace with Prataparudra Gajapati - battles, terms  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Prataparudra Gajapati's daughter, given in marriage to Krishnadevaraya, is identified in the sources by which set of names?
o: Bhadradevi, Tukkadevi and Jaganmohini; also Annapurnadevi
accepted.x: The daughter is referred to as Bhadradevi, Tukkadevi or Jaganmohini, and also as Annapurnadevi.
accepted.tq: Recognise alternate names for the same historical person instead of treating them as separate princesses.
accepted.sec: Wars and peace with Prataparudra Gajapati - battles, terms  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the peace terms, Prataparudra Gajapati retained his position as a:
accepted.x: The lands north of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati, who continued as a feudatory.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a subordinate political status from independent kingship and military office.
accepted.sec: Wars and peace with Prataparudra Gajapati - battles, terms  [other exams, GROUP-II]

Only the royal family and battlefield weapons

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly presents the first and second usurpations and the last Tuluva ruler?
o: First—Saluva Narasimha in 1485; second—Vira Narasimha in 1505; last Tuluva ruler—Sadasiva
First—Vira Narasimha in 1505; second—Saluva Narasimha in 1485; last Tuluva ruler—Achyutaraya
First—Saluva Narasimha in 1505; second—Sadasiva in 1565; last Tuluva ruler—Vira Narasimha
First—Achyutaraya in 1529; second—Rama Raya in 1543; last Tuluva ruler—Krishnadevaraya
accepted.x: The first usurpation was by Saluva Narasimha in 1485, the second by Vira Narasimha in 1505, and Sadasiva was the last Tuluva ruler.
accepted.tq: Use the first-versus-second sequence and the dynastic endpoint to eliminate reversed combinations.
